channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Brussels is funding the voices that tell it what it wants to hear
item.description: Brussels’ nicotine debate has a transparency problem when public money funds organisations that then echo the Commission’s preferred line. The article points to a “market freeze” backed by several health ministers that would restrict future nicotine products while cigarettes remain available. That should concern anyone interested in evidence-based regulation. Public health policy needs independent scrutiny, consumer voices and open funding trails — especially when decisions could limit lower-risk alternatives for millions of adults who smoke. (Published on October 13, 2026bybrusselstimes.com)

item.title: CAPHRA Welcomes Oz Proposal
item.description: CAPHRA welcomes an Australian opposition proposal to legalise and regulate adult access to vapes and nicotine pouches without prescriptions, but warns against linking it to an 80% cigarette excise cut. The package includes $200 million for enforcement and is projected to raise $8 billion over four years. Australia’s government rejects the proposal, while public health groups warn cheaper cigarettes could increase smoking. CAPHRA argues regulated alternatives—not cheaper cigarettes—would address illicit markets, citing New Zealand’s declining smoking rates since vaping regulation. It urges Canberra to assess legalisation separately from the contentious cigarette tax debate. (Published on October 14, 2026byplanetofthevapes.co.uk)

item.title: THR Doesn’t Need Nicotine to Be Innocent
item.description: Tobacco harm reduction does not require nicotine to be innocent. It requires honesty about where the greatest harm comes from. Nicotine can cause dependence and should not be promoted casually, but cigarettes are deadly because they burn tobacco and expose users to toxic smoke. The case for safer nicotine products rests on reducing that exposure — not on pretending nicotine has no risks. (Published on October 14, 2026bysubstack.com)
